questions.prompt: Bonevac’s two grand Western traditions are framed as footnotes to:
Descartes’s cogito-style move says even if I am wrong that I exist:
choices: B Someone must exist to be wrong/doubt—thinking/doubting secures that I am a thinking thing.
C Only the body is certain.

questions.prompt: Rationalists grant much knowledge from experience but insist some is:
choices: B Independent of experience—innate / inborn structure of mind.
C Only habit with no structure.
D Purely animal instinct without concepts.

questions.prompt: Leibniz treats concepts like unity/substance/objecthood as:
choices: B Built into the structure of our minds.
D Derived solely from utility calculations.

questions.prompt: “Synthetic a priori” names truths that are:
choices: A Merely verbal and about the world only by definition.
B About the world (synthetic) yet knowable independent of experience (a priori).
